papers.key_finding: Habitually barefoot runners typically land forefoot/midfoot and avoid the impact transient (collision spike) of rearfoot strikers; how the foot lands shapes impact loading more than footwear alone. Backs scoring foot strike together with overstride, never heel contact alone.
papers.title: Foot strike patterns and collision forces in habitually barefoot versus shod runners

papers.key_finding: Increasing step rate a little above preferred at constant speed lowers hip and knee joint loading. The evidence behind the cadence cue (+5-10%) and strict knees-zone scoring.
papers.title: Effects of step rate manipulation on joint mechanics during running

papers.journal: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Clinics of North America
papers.key_finding: Evidence-based framework for videotaped running analysis: which deviations are visible from which camera view and how they link to injury. The direct model for the 7-zone, view-dependent (side/front) judgeability matrix.
papers.title: An evidence-based videotaped running biomechanics analysis

papers.key_finding: Collegiate cross-country runners who habitually rearfoot-struck had roughly twice the rate of repetitive-stress injuries as forefoot strikers. Backs flagging rearfoot-plus-overstride landings in the feet_strike zone.
papers.title: Foot strike and injury rates in endurance runners: a retrospective study

papers.key_finding: Measured ground reaction forces across foot-strike styles in distance runners; strike-index classification of rear/mid/forefoot contact. The measurement basis for the feet_strike zone and why strike pattern changes force profiles.
papers.title: Ground reaction forces in distance running

papers.key_finding: Systematic review: lower-extremity running-injury incidence 19-79% with the knee the predominant site; prior injury and high weekly mileage are risk factors. Justifies strict knee-zone scoring and honest score caps.
papers.title: Incidence and determinants of lower extremity running injuries in long distance runners: a systematic review

papers.key_finding: Injured runners vs controls: greater contralateral pelvic drop, more forward trunk lean at midstance, more extended knee and more ankle dorsiflexion at initial contact. Directly backs hips_pelvis, trunk_lean, knees and feet_strike scoring.
papers.title: Is there a pathological gait associated with common soft tissue running injuries?

papers.key_finding: Systematic review: increasing stride rate (shortening stride) consistently reduces impact loading, braking impulse and joint excursion. Backs the cadence cue and knees/feet_strike fixes.
papers.title: Influence of stride frequency and length on running mechanics: a systematic review

papers.key_finding: Meta-analysis: rearfoot striking imposes higher overall impact and knee/patellofemoral loads while forefoot striking shifts load to the ankle, with no economy advantage either way. Backs zone-specific strike advice, not one-size-fits-all.
papers.title: Effects of foot strike techniques on running biomechanics: a systematic review and meta-analysis

papers.key_finding: Systematic review of injury-specific biomechanical risk factors: overuse injuries arise from an interplay of training load and individual mechanics (kinematics, ground reaction forces, loading rates). Backs per-zone scoring tied to specific mechanisms, not a single global score.
papers.title: Running-related biomechanical risk factors for overuse injuries in distance runners: a systematic review considering injury specificity and the potentials for future research

papers.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy
papers.key_finding: A ~7-degree increase in forward trunk lean significantly lowered patellofemoral joint stress; an upright trunk raised kneecap load. Backs scoring trunk_lean from the ankles and cueing slight forward lean for knee complaints.
papers.title: Sagittal plane trunk posture influences patellofemoral joint stress during running
